q: Do we count our own aluminium scrap that we remelt in our cast house in the CBAM figure?
title: Remelting your own aluminium scrap in CBAM
short: Not as a precursor. Scrap made and remelted inside your own installation is part of your own production loop: count the fuel used to remelt it, and do not add the scrap again as an input. Count only aluminium that leaves as product.
audience: Extruders, rolling mills and foundries with in-house cast houses

p: Internal scrap was already counted when the metal first entered the installation. Adding it again as an input would double count the same aluminium.

ul: Fuel for remelting furnaces and holding furnaces.
Unwrought aluminium bought in, as a precursor.
Scrap bought from outside, which carries zero embedded emissions.

p: Track metal in and out of the cast house: purchased ingot, outside scrap, internal scrap and finished output. A simple monthly balance shows the verifier nothing is counted twice.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and production documents into dated, fingerprinted installation records, the starting point for the actual emissions an EU importer asks for.
